incidental

/in-sih-DEN-tl/ - rhymes with dental · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incidental means occurring as a minor accompaniment; of secondary importance.

The theater program credits ten minutes of incidental music — small phrases that cover the scene changes.

Worked Example

The bookshop's espresso counter brings in incidental income: pleasant on a slow Tuesday, and the owner would defend the machine with her life. But the ledger tells the truth — ninety-two cents of every dollar still comes from books. The counter rides along; the shelves pay the rent.

Incidental is exact because it ranks, it doesn't insult. The espresso money is real; it simply accompanies the main business instead of being it. Something incidental happens alongside and matters less — remove it and the enterprise walks on unbothered.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

minor: Minor measures size or importance in any setting: a minor scrape, a minor cost, a minor delay. Incidental says something more specific — the thing is small because it merely accompanies the main matter. A minor repair can still be central to the day; an incidental one just rides along.

secondary: Secondary means ranked behind the main thing but still counted among the goals — a mission's secondary objective is still an objective somebody planned for. Incidental sits outside the ranking altogether: it was never one of the goals, only something that happens alongside them.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

central: at the heart of the matter

principal: first in rank — the thing itself

Where it sits · how much the whole depends on it — incidental → supporting → indispensable

supporting vs. incidental: A supporting part already outranks an incidental one: the show leans on its supporting cast, while an incidental touch could vanish unmissed.

indispensable vs. incidental: Indispensable crowns the ladder — the show cannot go on without it — a full climb above the incidental, which merely rides along.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: upon

Root — cid-

Root — cid-: to fall (Latin cadere)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: -ing; doing

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: In- (upon) + cid- (to fall) + -ent + -al = falling upon, falling in alongside. Latin incidere described what falls onto a path while you walk it. An incidental expense, melody, or remark is exactly that: something that falls in beside the main event without ever becoming it.

Use the root in a new word: coincidence

Use the root in a new word: coincidence: By pure coincidence, both cousins booked the same tiny hostel in Lisbon for the same week.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / academic

Incidental ranks things: present, genuine, but riding alongside the main matter. Extraneous, its unit-mate, expels things: imported from outside the matter altogether. The bookshop's espresso income is incidental — it belongs to the shop. A poster's pet timeline is extraneous — it belongs to another subject entirely. Choose by whether the thing belongs at all.
